Pearl (PRL): real proof-of-useful-work tech, a token priced ahead of its usage

Deep dive on Pearl, the matrix-multiplication proof-of-work chain: on-chain data, holder and pool concentration, emissions, liquidity, the hype cycle on X, and bear/base/bull scenarios. Research only.

Research only. Not financial advice. All times are ET (UTC-4). Labeling rule for this note: every hashrate, supply and market cap figure is marked unconfirmed. Each still carries its source, but none of them has been independently confirmed. Hashrate is an explorer estimate derived from difficulty. Supply comes from an explorer and an aggregator, cross-checked against the emission formula. Market cap is an aggregator figure on thin venues. Charts and diagrams: every chart is built only from the raw pulls saved for this note, and each caption names its source and fetch time (ET). Diagrams are simplified schematics.

Price line (refreshed): PRL $1.11 on CoinGecko (last updated 2026-10-02 16:06 ET), 24h change -5.5%, 24h volume $4.80M. The OpenBB yfinance PRL41876-USD daily bar for Oct 2 (run at 16:07:31 ET, bar still open) read $1.1145. Market cap $368.7M (CoinGecko, 16:06 ET, unconfirmed). Fully diluted value is about $2.33B at the 2.1B max supply (derived, unconfirmed).

The call in one paragraph

Pearl is the most serious proof-of-useful-work design we have reviewed, and the team is unusually credible. The token is a different question. It has re-rated about 4x to 5x on narrative since late August. On-chain usage has roughly doubled, and fees are close to zero. Usefulness is enabled by the protocol but not enforced. Supply grows about 27% in three months and about 92% in twelve. Reported spot liquidity sits on two low-trust venues. On our read, attention peaked around Sep 27. Our research view at about $1.11 is avoid an outright long (medium conviction). The bull case depends almost entirely on the FP8 / Pearl-GEMM upgrade shipping and on verifiable demand for useful mining.

What Pearl is

Pearl is a proof-of-work Layer 1 derived from Bitcoin. Mainnet launched 2026-04-27. It replaces SHA-256 with noised matrix multiplication, so GPU work that serves AI inference can mine PRL at the same time. Pearl calls this "duplex compute". The core construction is in arXiv 2504.09971. Max supply is 2.1B PRL, with a smooth emission curve that puts half the supply out by block 650,226. Hashrate Index describes "roughly two-minute blocks" and a "2.1 billion PRL max supply". The explorer reports a 194 second target.

  • Team: Omri Weinstein (ex-Nvidia, Vast Data), Ilan Komargodski, Idan Sugerman. Rafael Pass is research scientist and advisor (economics paper arXiv 2606.06700). The team claims no premine and no VC token allocation.
  • Code: the GitHub repo was created 2026-04-19 and was active on Oct 2 (335 stars, 79 forks, 95 open issues, read about 11:46 ET). Recent releases: v1.4.1 (Aug 11, emergency "Salted noise-seed" hardfork), v1.4.8 (Sep 16), v1.4.11 (Sep 29). Three committers since Sep 1. The FP8 pull request (#311) was still open.
  • Partner: Together AI's May 15 blog announced an "exclusive partnership". It said the Gemma-4-31B-it-Pearl endpoint "is discounted by over 25%, offset by the future value of crypto emissions" (page re-saved 16:07 ET). The model page lists $0.28 input and $0.86 output per 1M tokens (INT8, 32K context). The same page states "This model is not available on Together's Serverless API" (re-saved 16:07 ET). So the discount is real on paper, but live availability is unclear.
  • Pearl's own inference product at pearlresearch.ai is priced in USD, not PRL. Today there is no token sink.

Market structure

All of the following are CoinGecko figures as of 11:44 ET unless stated.

  • Price $1.13. Market cap $373M (unconfirmed). FDV $2.36B (unconfirmed). Rank 133. ATH $1.76 on Sep 23 (01:19 ET). ATL $0.1399 on Jul 22 (21:44 ET). 30-day change +252%.
  • Price path (CoinGecko daily): $0.509 on Jul 1, $0.230 on Jul 23 after the July exploit, $0.270 on Aug 10, $0.310 on Aug 31, $0.470 on Sep 10, $1.072 on Sep 18, $1.534 on Sep 27, $1.126 on Oct 2. Market cap was $68.9M to $79.0M through August (unconfirmed). That matches the "$70 to 80 million" claim in the Sep 10 brezshares thesis.
  • Venues: BigONE PRL/USDT $2.47M and SafeTrade PRL/USDT $1.68M of 24h volume, with null CoinGecko trust scores. CoinPaprika (11:46 ET) lists SafeTrade only, at $1.81M. Uniswap WPRL/USDT has $397k of reserves and $165k of 24h volume (GeckoTerminal 11:50 ET). @headroomcapital measured about $5k to $8k of depth within ±2% on SafeTrade (X, unverified).
  • Liquidity vs peers: PRL's 24h volume-to-market-cap ratio was 0.011. That is the lowest in our comparison set (TAO 0.071, RENDER 0.056, ZEC 0.053, AKT 0.034). It is priced like a mid-cap and trades like a micro-cap.
  • Behavior (OpenBB yfinance, Aug 20 to Oct 2, run 11:53 ET): PRL returned +319% against BTC +17%, TAO +44% and RENDER +41%. Annualized volatility was 242%, versus 42% for BTC. Correlation of daily returns with BTC was 0.28, with TAO 0.17 and with RENDER -0.02. PRL trades on its own flows.

Margin.Trade has offered 3x PRL perps since June. On Hyperliquid, ticker-bot text quoted by @degennQuant (Sep 26) says the HIP-3 "pearl-2:native ticker has been purchased for 554.89 HYPE ($51,016) by @entropyIO" (X, unverified). A separate @HyperliquidNews post from Jun 29 concerns a spot "$PRL" ticker bought for 500 HYPE. It is a different event, and it may not even be Pearl. We found no confirmation that the HIP-3 market has launched. There is no Binance, OKX or Coinbase listing.

On-chain picture

Sources: the pearlchain.live keyless API, fetched 11:45 ET. The official Blockbook reported the same height, 122,270. Wallet classifications below are behavioral inferences, because no public labels exist.

  • Hashrate used in this note: about 43.7 EH/s (unconfirmed). It comes from pearlchain.live at 11:45 ET, which labels it "difficulty-derived ... not measured computation". All other hashrate figures below are explorer history samples or X claims, labeled as such.
  • Supply: 15.83% minted, about 332.4M PRL (unconfirmed; explorer and CoinGecko, matching the emission formula). The block reward is 2,288 PRL. The explorer's address total of 342.9M is about 3% higher than this, and we could not reconcile the gap.
  • Issuance: about 1.02M to 1.07M PRL per day (unconfirmed). Oct 1 was 1,065,348 PRL. At the refreshed CoinGecko price of $1.11 (16:06 ET), Oct 1 issuance is worth about $1.18M. That is about 25% of CoinGecko's 24h volume of $4.80M at the same timestamp. At current run rates, issuance is about 115% of supply per year.
  • Dilution path (emission formula, unconfirmed): about 421M PRL around Jan 2 to 5, 2027, about 500M around Apr 2 to 8, 2027, and about 640M around Oct 2 to 16, 2027. At today's market cap of $368.7M (unconfirmed), price would be about $0.88 at 421M supply and about $0.58 at 640M. Holding $1.11 at 640M supply needs about a $710M market cap (unconfirmed, derived).
  • Holder concentration: the top 10 addresses hold 15.2% of tracked supply, the top 100 hold 43.8% and the top 1,000 hold 75.8%. Forty-two addresses with at least 1M PRL each hold 33.6%.
  • Large holders: of the top 25 wallets, 17 (60.2M PRL, unconfirmed) have never sent a coin. Three of those are pure launch-era miner wallets, holding 9.9M combined and dormant since May. Several others received round-number deposits, which fits OTC buyers or cold storage. The largest address (8.18M PRL) was created by a consolidation of hundreds of inputs at 04:22 ET on Oct 2. Its owner is unknown. No exchange, team or treasury wallet can be identified from public data.
  • Launch distribution: 125.1M PRL, 37.6% of current supply (unconfirmed), was mined Apr 27 to May 3. That was before the public miner shipped on May 15, while hashrate was under about 1 EH/s. This is not a premine, but it is a real fairness and concentration caveat.
  • Pool concentration: over the last 200 blocks (Oct 1 23:41 ET to Oct 2 11:34 ET), one payout address found 51% of blocks, and the top three found 84%. Both of the largest payees forward nearly everything they mine, which is typical of pools. Pool names could not be mapped.
  • Hashrate history (explorer samples, unconfirmed): 0.31 EH/s on Apr 30, about 24 on Jun 2, 70.3 on Jul 23, then 17 on Jul 26 after the MoE exploit patch. A 143.3 EH/s sample on Aug 11 came during a spoofing exploit and the block 99,000 hardfork. After that: 41.3 on Sep 21, 59.2 on Sep 27, 43.6 on Oct 2. Two X claims do not match these samples and are unverified. @CryptoSGiants (Jul 23) says "roughly half" of a 90+ EH/s peak came from an exploit. @degennQuant (Sep 27 11:51 ET) says "hashrate crosses 60.85 EH/s".
  • Activity: average daily transactions by month were 21,519 in June, 8,792 in August and 15,479 in September. Average daily active addresses were 25,037 in June, 11,327 in August and 16,899 in September. The all-time high was 40,375 active addresses on May 29. In the last 200 blocks, 60% were coinbase-only, and much of the non-coinbase activity is pool payouts.
  • Fees: about 7,187 PRL all time, roughly 0.002% of issuance. No fee time series is exposed.
  • Wrapped PRL: WPRL on Ethereum (PearlBridge, an upgradeable proxy) has 2.0M tokens outstanding, about 0.6% of supply, and 2,676 holders (Ethplorer 11:50 ET).
  • Ticker collision: DexScreener (12:13 ET) shows several other PRL tokens: Perle on Solana and BSC, Parallel, and copycat "Pearl" ERC-20s on Base created Sep 18 and Sep 22. Verify contracts before relying on any "$PRL" data.

Miner economics

  • Revenue: at $1.11, issuance is about $1.13M to $1.19M per day (unconfirmed issuance).
  • Cost anchors: prlstats.com (@jeremiahrogers, Sep 26, at about 59 EH/s) estimated $2.24 per PRL for synthetic mining on frontier hardware, $0.68 on idle owned GPUs and $1.31 during inference. arXiv 2606.04819 (June, 24 EH/s, PRL at $0.76) put breakeven at $0.46 to $0.77 by GPU tier.
  • Scaled to today: scaling the prlstats figures to the unconfirmed 43.7 EH/s gives roughly $1.66, $0.50 and $0.97 (derived).
  • Read: the marginal rented miner is near breakeven at today's price. Owned hardware has much lower cash costs, so most issuance is likely sold whatever the price. Together's own framing, an endpoint discount "offset by the future value of crypto emissions", implies the same thing for duplex miners.
  • Overhead: @WeinsteinOmri says the current protocol is "INT-8 only, and adds 10-15% overhead". The new Pearl-GEMM targets 0 to 3% and is "expected to launch within weeks". He also says it "will always allow spam mining". arXiv 2606.04819 found no inference strings in the dominant pool's mining software (May 30 to 31).

Hype on X: what the attention data shows

Method: we drew a day-by-day sample of X posts mentioning Pearl, Apr 20 to Oct 2, collected 11:57 to 12:12 ET. It yielded 5,622 posts, of which 2,475 were Pearl-specific. On top of that we read about 75 posts in full. Counts are a sample, not a census.

  • Two waves. Wave 1 was driven by mining returns. It started with the Together launch (May 15) and Chinese GPU-rental mining guides, and peaked May 28. Active addresses peaked the next day. Price then fell 67% from Jun 25 to Jul 23 (CoinGecko). Wave 2 has been led by investors and influencers since the brezshares thesis on Sep 10 ("@nolimithodl has been aggressively accumulating", a disclosed position). It was amplified by @degennQuant and talk of perp listings. Post counts and price both peaked on Sep 27.
  • Late-cycle signals. Median views per Pearl post fell from 850 to 2,461 on most days of Sep 14 to 23 to 50 to 186 since Sep 25. The bullish share of views fell from 27% (Sep 16 to 30) to 5% on Oct 1 and 2 (small sample). Price is down about 20% from the Sep 27 Yahoo close.
  • Who drives reach. Since Sep 1, @brezshares (disclosed holder) and @degennQuant (no disclosure in post text) account for about 25% of Pearl-post views. @margin_trade, a venue promoting its own PRL perps, ran #LongPRL posts. We found no evidence of a bot or copy-paste campaign.
  • Claims check. - "Exclusive" Together deal: the wording is verified. The terms are not public, and the deal dates from May 15, not October. - "3 to 5% overhead": misleading for today's mainnet (10 to 15% per the CEO). - "Mining is real AI": contradicted by the arXiv evidence. - "a16z wallet accumulating" (@optimist: "allegedly"), Ribbit Capital investment, and "Ansem shilling": all unverified. - "$PRL top gainer on Solana": that refers to Perle, a different token.
  • Hype vs use. From the Aug 24 week to the Sep 21 week, Pearl posts rose 22x and price rose 5.0x. Active addresses rose 1.9x and transactions 2.3x. Fees stayed close to zero.

Catalysts and risks

Catalysts:

  1. FP8 / Pearl-GEMM hardfork. Described as "within weeks", with no date. This is the main fundamental catalyst.
  2. Hyperliquid HIP-3 perp launch. Two-sided: it brings attention, but also a liquid venue for miner hedging and for short sellers.
  3. A tier-1 exchange listing. None confirmed.
  4. More duplex partners, or Together's endpoint becoming clearly live.
  5. Attestable proof of what share of hashrate does useful work.

Risks:

  • Dilution: +27% supply in 3 months and +92% in 12 (unconfirmed supply).
  • Thin, low-trust venues.
  • Pool concentration: one payee found 51% of recent blocks.
  • Launch-week supply concentration.
  • Rentable, merge-mined hashrate, and two consensus exploits so far.
  • An upgradeable bridge.
  • Promotion-driven flows.
  • Ticker collisions.

What would change the view

Bullish falsifiers:

  • FP8 live on mainnet with measured end-to-end overhead of 3% or less, and within about 60 days attestable data showing over 30% of hashrate doing paid inference.
  • A second named production duplex partner.
  • PRL holding above $1.80 for five daily closes after a Hyperliquid listing.
  • Fees above 1% of block rewards over 30 days.

Bearish confirmations:

  • FP8 not on mainnet by Dec 31, 2026.
  • A single payee above 50% over 1,000 blocks.
  • Non-coinbase transactions under 10,000 per day while price holds.
  • Large dormant wallets moving to venues.

Scenarios (research only, subjective probabilities)

These scenarios use supply of about 421M at 3 months and about 640M at 12 months (unconfirmed).

  • 3 months, bear (40%): $0.35 to $0.70. FP8 slips, miners keep selling into thin volume, and price reverts toward miner cost anchors.
  • 3 months, base (40%): $0.80 to $1.40. FP8 is announced but not decisive. Market cap grows slower than supply.
  • 3 months, bull (20%): $1.80 to $3.00. FP8 ships on time with a tier-1 listing or a liquid perp, plus a second duplex partner.
  • 12 months, bear (45%): $0.15 to $0.45. Usefulness stays unproven, and supply roughly doubles into fading attention.
  • 12 months, base (35%): $0.50 to $1.10. FP8 is live with some duplex adoption, but per-coin value is diluted.
  • 12 months, bull (20%): $2.00 to $5.00. Duplex becomes the dominant mining mode, with multiple partners and tier-1 listings.

Probability-weighted midpoints are about $1.08 at 3 months and about $1.02 at 12 months. These midpoints are geometric, not arithmetic: each range is represented by the square root of its low times its high, rounded ($0.50, $1.05 and $2.30 at 3 months; $0.30, $0.80 and $3.00 at 12 months). Unrounded geometric midpoints give about $1.09 and $1.01. Arithmetic midpoints would give about $1.13 and $1.12. Both sit near or slightly below spot, with a fat right tail. That shape is why the research view is to avoid a long rather than to take a high-conviction short. Short-side risk is high: low float, headline-driven moves of +30% to +50% in a day (Yahoo closes Sep 10 to 11 and Sep 17 to 18), and positive perp funding that can flip.

Data we could not get

  • Exchange, team and pool wallet labels.
  • A fee time series.
  • Coin-age and dormancy distribution. This needs our own node and indexer.
  • Order-book depth from SafeTrade and BigONE directly.
  • Hyperliquid HIP-3 launch status.
  • CoinMarketCap (not checked).
